from django.utils.timesince import timesince
import django

# Configure settings for the reproduction script

    settings.configure(
        USE_TZ=True,
        SECRET_KEY='dummy',

    )

def test_long_interval_with_tz():
    try:
        now = timezone.now()
        d = now - datetime.timedelta(days=31)
        print(f"Now: {now}")
        print(f"D: {d}")
        result = timesince(d)
        print(f"Result: {result}")
        print("Success!")
    except TypeError as e:
        print(f"Caught TypeError: {e}")
        raise e
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Caught unexpected exception: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        raise e

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_long_interval_with_tz()

from django.db.models import Index, UniqueConstraint, CheckConstraint, Q
from django.contrib.postgres.constraints import ExclusionConstraint

def test_reprs():
    idx = Index(fields=['f1', 'f2'], name='idx_name', condition=Q(f1__gt=0), include=['f3'], opclasses=['op1', 'op2'])
    print(f"Index: {repr(idx)}")

    idx_expr = Index(expressions=[Q(f1__gt=0)], name='idx_expr_name')
    print(f"Index (expr): {repr(idx_expr)}")

    uc = UniqueConstraint(fields=['f1', 'f2'], name='uc_name', condition=Q(f1__gt=0), include=['f3'], opclasses=['op1', 'op2'])
    print(f"UniqueConstraint: {repr(uc)}")

    cc = CheckConstraint(check=Q(f1__gt=0), name='cc_name')
    print(f"CheckConstraint: {repr(cc)}")

    ec = ExclusionConstraint(expressions=[('f1', '=')], name='ec_name', index_type='GIST', condition=Q(f1__gt=0), include=['f3'], opclasses=['varchar_pattern_ops'])
    print(f"ExclusionConstraint: {repr(ec)}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_reprs()

import os
import time
import django
from django.conf import settings
from django.db.models import Prefetch

if not settings.configured:
    settings.configure(
        DATABASES={
            'default': {
                'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.sqlite3',
                'NAME': 'test_db.sqlite3',
            }
        },
        INSTALLED_APPS=[
            'myapp',
        ],
    )
    django.setup()

from myapp.models import Machine, OperatingSystem, Identifier
from django.db.models.query import QuerySet

def setup_data(num_machines=100, num_os=1, num_ids=2):
    print(f"Setting up {num_machines} machines...")
    os_objs = [OperatingSystem.objects.create(name=f"OS {i}") for i in range(10)]
    
    machines = []
    for i in range(num_machines):
        m = Machine.objects.create(name=f"Machine {i}")
        m.operating_systems.add(os_objs[i % 10])
        machines.append(m)
    
    for m in machines:
        for j in range(num_ids):
            Identifier.objects.create(name=f"ID {m.id}-{j}", machine=m)
    print("Data setup complete.")

def test_prefetch_correctness():
    print("Testing prefetch correctness...")
    # Test ManyToMany
    m = Machine.objects.prefetch_related('operating_systems').first()
    os_qs = m.operating_systems.all()
    assert isinstance(os_qs, QuerySet)
    assert len(os_qs) > 0
    
    # Test Reverse ManyToOne
    m = Machine.objects.prefetch_related('identifiers').first()
    id_qs = m.identifiers.all()
    assert isinstance(id_qs, QuerySet)
    assert len(id_qs) > 0
    
    # Test filtered prefetch
    first_machine = Machine.objects.first()
    id_name = first_machine.identifiers.all()[0].name
    
    machines = Machine.objects.prefetch_related(
        Prefetch('identifiers', queryset=Identifier.objects.filter(name=id_name))
    ).all()
    
    for m in machines:
        ids = m.identifiers.all()
        assert isinstance(ids, QuerySet)
        if m == first_machine:
            assert len(ids) == 1
            assert ids[0].name == id_name
        else:
            assert len(ids) == 0
    
    print("Correctness tests passed!")

def test_performance():
    # Use a larger number of machines for performance test
    print("Testing performance...")
    start_time = time.time()
    machines = Machine.objects.prefetch_related('operating_systems', 'identifiers').all()
    for m in machines:
        # Just accessing them to ensure they are prefetched
        list(m.operating_systems.all())
        list(m.identifiers.all())
    end_time = time.time()
    print(f"Prefetch took: {end_time - start_time:.4f} seconds")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Clean up DB for each run
    import os
    if os.path.exists('test_db.sqlite3'):
        os.remove('test_db.sqlite3')
    
    # Redo migrations because we deleted the DB
    import subprocess
    subprocess.run(['python3', 'manage.py', 'migrate'], check=True)
    
    setup_data(num_machines=5000)
    test_prefetch_correctness()
    test_performance()

import os
import django
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models
from django.db.models import Sum, F, OuterRef, Subquery, Case, When, FloatField, Count
from django.db.models.functions import Round

# Configure settings
if not settings.configured:
    settings.configure(
        DATABASES={
            'default': {
                'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.sqlite3',
                'NAME': ':memory:',
            }
        },
        INSTALLED_APPS=[
            'reproduce_issue',
        ],
    )
    django.setup()

from reproduce_issue.models import Author, Book

# Create tables
with django.db.connection.schema_editor() as schema_editor:
    schema_editor.create_model(Author)
    schema_editor.create_model(Book)

# Create test data
a1 = Author.objects.create(name="Author A")
a2 = Author.objects.create(name="Author B")
a3 = Author.objects.create(name="Author C")

Book.objects.create(title="Book 1", author=a1)
Book.objects.create(title="Book 2", author=a1)
Book.objects.create(title="Book 3", author=a2)
# a3 has no books

print("Data created.")

total_books_qs = (
    Book.objects.filter(author__pk=OuterRef("pk"))
    .order_by()
    .values("pk")
    .annotate(total=Count("pk"))
    .values("total")
)

annotated_authors = Author.objects.annotate(
    total_books=Subquery(total_books_qs.annotate(
            total_books=F("total")
    ).values("total_books")),
    total_books_a=Subquery(total_books_qs.filter(
        author__name__istartswith="a"
    ).annotate(
            total_books_a=F("total")
    ).values("total_books_a")),
).values(
    "pk",
    "total_books",
    "total_books_a",
).order_by("-total_books")

print("Annotated authors query created.")

try:
    totals = annotated_authors.aggregate(
        sum_total_books=Sum("total_books"),
        sum_total_books_a=Sum("total_books_a"),
        a_over_total_rate=Case(
            When(
                sum_total_books=0,
                then=0,
            ),
            default=Round(
                (Sum("total_books_a") / Sum("total_books")) * 100, 2
            ),
            output_field=FloatField(),
        ),
    )
    print("Aggregate result:", totals)
except Exception as e:
    print("Caught exception:", e)
    import traceback
    traceback.print_exc()

from astropy.cosmology.connect import readwrite_registry
from astropy.cosmology.core import Cosmology
from astropy.table import QTable
from .table import to_table

# Mapping of Cosmology parameter names to LaTeX labels.
LATEX_MAPPING = {
    "name": "Name",
    "H0": r"$H_0 \rm{ [km (Mpc s)^{-1}]}$",
    "Om0": r"$\Omega_{m,0}$",
    "Ob0": r"$\Omega_{b,0}$",
    "Tcmb0": r"$T_{\mathrm{CMB},0} \rm{ [K]}$",
    "Neff": r"$N_{\mathrm{eff}}$",
    "m_nu": r"$\sum m_\nu \rm{ [eV]}$",
}

def write_latex(cosmology, file, *, cls=QTable, cosmology_in_meta=True, **kwargs):
    """Serialize the cosmology into a LaTeX table.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cosmology : `~astropy.cosmology.Cosmology` subclass instance
    file : path-like or file-like
        Location to save the serialized cosmology.
    cls : type (optional, keyword-only)
        Astropy :class:`~astropy.table.Table` (sub)class to use when writing.
        Default is :class:`~astropy.table.QTable`.
    cosmology_in_meta : bool
        Whether to put the cosmology class in the Table metadata (if `True`,
        default) or as the first column (if `False`).
    **kwargs
        Passed to ``cls.write``
    """
    table = to_table(cosmology, cls=cls, cosmology_in_meta=cosmology_in_meta)

    # Format column names for LaTeX
    new_colnames = [LATEX_MAPPING.get(col, col) for col in table.colnames]
    table.colnames = new_colnames

    kwargs["format"] = "latex"
    table.write(file, **kwargs)

def latex_identify(origin, filepath, fileobj, *args, **kwargs):
    """Identify if object uses the LaTeX format.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
    """
    return filepath is not None and filepath.endswith((".tex", ".latex"))

# ===================================================================
# Register

readwrite_registry.register_writer("latex", Cosmology, write_latex)
readwrite_registry.register_identifier("latex", Cosmology, latex_identify)

import signal
import subprocess

from django.core.files.temp import NamedTemporaryFile
from django.db.backends.base.client import BaseDatabaseClient


def _escape_pgpass(txt):
    """
    Escape a fragment of a PostgreSQL .pgpass file.
    """
    return txt.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace(':', '\\:')


class DatabaseClient(BaseDatabaseClient):
    executable_name = 'psql'

    @classmethod
    def runshell_db(cls, conn_params):
        args = [cls.executable_name]

        host = conn_params.get('host', '')
        port = conn_params.get('port', '')
        dbname = conn_params.get('database', '')
        user = conn_params.get('user', '')
        passwd = conn_params.get('password', '')

        if user:
            args += ['-U', user]
        if host:
            args += ['-h', host]
        if port:
            args += ['-p', str(port)]
        args += [dbname]

        env = os.environ.copy()
        if passwd:
            env['PGPASSWORD'] = passwd

        sigint_handler = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGINT)
        try:
            # Allow SIGINT to pass to psql to abort queries.
            signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal.SIG_IGN)
            subprocess.run(args, env=env, check=True)
        finally:
            # Restore the original SIGINT handler.
            signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, sigint_handler)

    def runshell(self):
        DatabaseClient.runshell_db(self.connection.get_connection_params())

        'repro_pkg.subA.Foo': ObjectEntry('index', 'repro_pkg.subA.Foo', 'class', True),

        'repro_pkg.subB.Bar.somename': ObjectEntry('index', 'repro_pkg.subB.Bar.somename', 'attr', True),
    }

    # Test fuzzy search for 'somename'
    # We want to see what find_obj returns.
    # modname=None, clsname=None, name='somename', type=None, searchmode=1
    
    # Simulate the fuzzy search path in find_obj
    name = 'somename'
    objtypes = list(domain.object_types) # ['module', 'class', 'function', 'method', 'attribute', 'exception', 'data']
    # Wait, in Sphinx 4.0, objtypes are slightly different.
    # Let's check what domain.object_types is.
    
    # Actually, let's just pass the list of types we care about.
    objtypes = ['attr', 'class']

    # The code we are testing is in find_obj.
    # Since we want to test the FIX, we have to implement the FIX in the test and see if it works.
    
    def find_obj_original(modname, clsname, name, objtypes, searchmode):
        if searchmode == 1:
            searchname = '.' + name
            matches = [(oname, domain.objects[oname]) for oname in domain.objects
                       if oname.endswith(searchname) and
                       domain.objects[oname].objtype in objtypes]
            return matches
        return []

    def find_obj_fixed(modname, clsname, name, objtypes, searchmode):
        if searchmode == 1:
            searchname = '.' + name
            matches = [(oname, domain.objects[oname]) for oname in domain.objects
                       if oname.endswith(searchname) and
                       domain.objects[oname].objtype in objtypes and
                       not (domain.objects[oname].objtype == 'attr' and 
                            len(oname.split('.')) > 2 and # must have a parent and a module
                            oname.rsplit('.', 1)[0] in domain.objects and 
                            domain.objects[oname.rsplit('.', 1)[0]].objtype == 'class')]
            return matches
        return []

    print("Original matches:", find_obj_original(None, None, name, objtypes, 1))
    print("Fixed matches:", find_obj_fixed(None, None, name, objtypes, 1))

        def __init__(self, field):

    widget_uuid = widgets.ForeignKeyRawIdWidget(rel_uuid, admin.site)

import django
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django.conf import settings
from unittest.mock import patch

# Configure minimal Django settings
if not settings.configured:
    settings.configure()

class MyCommand(BaseCommand):
    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(title="subcommands",
                                         dest="subcommand",
                                         required=True)
        foo = subparsers.add_parser("foo")
        foo.set_defaults(method=self.on_foo_command)
        foo.add_argument("--bar")

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        print(f"Handle called with options: {options}")

    def on_foo_command(self, *args, **options):
        print(f"on_foo_command called with options: {options}")

def test_call_command_with_subparser_dest():
    # Create an instance of MyCommand
    cmd_instance = MyCommand()
    
    with patch('django.core.management.get_commands') as mock_get_commands:
        mock_get_commands.return_value = {'mycommand': cmd_instance}
        try:
            print("Trying: call_command('mycommand', 'foo', bar=True)")
            call_command('mycommand', 'foo', bar=True)
            print("Success!")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Caught exception: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()

    with patch('django.core.management.get_commands') as mock_get_commands:
        mock_get_commands.return_value = {'mycommand': cmd_instance}
        try:
            print("\nTrying: call_command('mycommand', subcommand='foo', bar=True)")
            call_command('mycommand', subcommand='foo', bar=True)
            print("Success!")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Caught exception: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_call_command_with_subparser_dest()

import os
import django
from django.conf import settings
from django.core import serializers
from django.db import connection

# Configure settings
if not settings.configured:
    settings.configure(
        DATABASES={
            'default': {
                'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.sqlite3',
                'NAME': ':memory:',
            }
        },
        INSTALLED_APPS=[
            'reproduce_app',
        ],
    )
    django.setup()

from reproduce_app.models import TestTagMaster, TestTag, Test

def run_test():
    # Create tables
    with connection.schema_editor() as schema_editor:
        schema_editor.create_model(TestTagMaster)
        schema_editor.create_model(TestTag)
        schema_editor.create_model(Test)
        schema_editor.create_model(Test.tags.through)

    try:
        tag_master = TestTagMaster.objects.create(name="master")
        tag = TestTag.objects.create(name="tag", master=tag_master)
        test = Test.objects.create(name="test")
        test.tags.add(tag)
        test.save()
        print("Setup complete. Now serializing...")
        serializers.serialize("json", [test])
        print("Serialization successful!")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Caught exception: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_test()

class CustomFKField(models.ForeignKey):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        kwargs['to'] = 'testapp.HardcodedModel'
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
    def deconstruct(self):
        name, path, args, kwargs = super().deconstruct()
        del kwargs["to"]
        return name, path, args, kwargs

def test_reproduction():
    before = ProjectState()
    before.add_model(ModelState('testapp', 'HardcodedModel', []))
    after = ProjectState()
    after.add_model(ModelState('testapp', 'HardcodedModel', []))
    after.add_model(ModelState('testapp', 'TestModel', [('custom', CustomFKField(on_delete=models.CASCADE))]))
    
    try:
        changes = MigrationAutodetector(before, after)._detect_changes()
        print("Successfully detected changes!")
        print(changes)
    except KeyError as e:
        print(f"Caught expected KeyError: {e}")
        raise e
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Caught unexpected exception: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        raise e

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_reproduction()
    except Exception:
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        exit(1)
    exit(0)

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.handlers.wsgi import WSGIHandler
from django.http import FileResponse

# Configure Django settings
if not settings.configured:
    settings.configure(
        DEFAULT_CHARSET='utf-8',

def test_file_wrapper_block_size():
    # Mock wsgi.file_wrapper
    def mock_file_wrapper(filelike, block_size=None):
        return (f"block_size={block_size}",)

    environ = {
        'wsgi.file_wrapper': mock_file_wrapper,
        'REQUEST_METHOD': 'GET',
        'PATH_INFO': '/test/',
        'wsgi.input': BytesIO(b''),
    }

    def start_response(status, headers):
        pass

    # Use a FileResponse with a custom block_size
    class CustomFileResponse(FileResponse):
        block_size = 12345

    file_content = BytesIO(b"some content")
    response = CustomFileResponse(file_content)
    
    handler = WSGIHandler()
    # We need to mock get_response to return our CustomFileResponse
    handler.get_response = lambda request: response

    result = handler(environ, start_response)
    
    # result should be the iterable returned by mock_file_wrapper
    # which contains the block_size
    result_list = list(result)
    assert len(result_list) == 1
    assert result_list[0] == "block_size=12345"
    print("Test passed!")

    try:
        test_file_wrapper_block_size()
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"Test failed: {e}")
    except Exception as e:

call:write_file{content:<|"|>    def drop_isel(self, indexers=None, *, errors="raise", **indexers_kwargs):
        """Drop index positions from this dataset.

        Parameters
        ----------
        indexers : mapping of hashable to Any
            Index positions to drop
        errors : {"raise", "ignore"}, optional
            If 'raise' (default), raises an IndexError error if
            any of the index positions passed are not
            in the dataset. If 'ignore', any given positions that are in the
            dataset are dropped and no error is raised.
        **indexers_kwargs : {dim: indexer, ...}, optional
            The keyword arguments form of ``dim`` and ``indexers``

        Returns
        -------
        dropped : Dataset
        """
        indexers = either_dict_or_kwargs(indexers, indexers_kwargs, "drop_isel")

        if errors not in ["raise", "ignore"]:
            raise ValueError('errors must be either "raise" or "ignore"')

        ds = self
        for dim, isel_for_dim in indexers.items():
            if dim not in ds.dims:
                if errors == "raise":
                    raise KeyError(f"dimension {dim!r} not found in dataset")
                elif errors == "ignore":
                    continue

            if utils.is_scalar(isel_for_dim):
                isel_for_dim = [isel_for_dim]
            isel_for_dim = np.asarray(isel_for_dim)

            dim_size = ds.dims[dim]
            normalized_isel = np.where(isel_for_dim < 0, isel_for_dim + dim_size, isel_for_dim)

            if errors == "raise":
                if np.any((normalized_isel < 0) | (normalized_isel >= dim_size)):
                    raise IndexError("index out of bounds")

            to_drop = normalized_isel[(normalized_isel >= 0) & (normalized_isel < dim_size)]
            keep_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(dim_size), to_drop)

            ds = ds.isel({dim: keep_indices})

        return ds

from sklearn.calibration import calibration_curve

def proposed_calibration_curve(y_true, y_prob, normalize=False, n_bins=5):
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true)
    y_prob = np.asarray(y_prob)

    if normalize:  # Normalize predicted values into interval [0, 1]
        y_prob = (y_prob - y_prob.min()) / (y_prob.max() - y_prob.min())
    elif y_prob.min() < 0 or y_prob.max() > 1:
        raise ValueError("y_prob has values outside [0, 1] and normalize is "
                         "set to False.")

    if isinstance(n_bins, (int, np.integer)):
        bins = np.linspace(0., 1. + 1e-8, n_bins + 1)
    else:
        bins = np.asarray(n_bins).astype(float)
        if bins.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError("n_bins must be an integer or a 1D array.")
        if len(bins) < 2:
            raise ValueError("n_bins must have at least 2 edges.")
        if not np.all(np.diff(bins) > 0):
            raise ValueError("n_bins must be monotonically increasing.")
        bins[-1] += 1e-8

    binids = np.digitize(y_prob, bins) - 1
    
    mask = (binids >= 0) & (binids < len(bins) - 1)
    y_true = y_true[mask]
    y_prob = y_prob[mask]
    binids = binids[mask]

    bin_sums = np.bincount(binids, weights=y_prob, minlength=len(bins) - 1)
    bin_true = np.bincount(binids, weights=y_true, minlength=len(bins) - 1)
    bin_total = np.bincount(binids, minlength=len(bins) - 1)

    nonzero = bin_total != 0
    prob_true = (bin_true[nonzero] / bin_total[nonzero])
    prob_pred = (bin_sums[nonzero] / bin_total[nonzero])

    return prob_true, prob_pred

# Test with integer n_bins
y_true = np.array([0, 1, 0, 1])
y_prob = np.array([0.1, 0.4, 0.6, 0.9])
n_bins = 2
res_old = calibration_curve(y_true, y_prob, n_bins=n_bins)
res_new = proposed_calibration_curve(y_true, y_prob, n_bins=n_bins)
print(f"Int n_bins match: {np.allclose(res_old[0], res_new[0]) and np.allclose(res_old[1], res_new[1])}")

# Test with array n_bins
my_bins = np.array([0, 0.2, 0.8, 1.0])
res_new_array = proposed_calibration_curve(y_true, y_prob, n_bins=my_bins)
print(f"Array n_bins result: prob_true={res_new_array[0]}, prob_pred={res_new_array[1]}")

# Manual check for array n_bins:
# bins: [0, 0.2), [0.2, 0.8), [0.8, 1.0]
# y_prob = [0.1, 0.4, 0.6, 0.9]
# bins:

# 0.6 -> bin 1. y_true=0, y_prob=0.6. Mean true=0.5, Mean prob=0.5

# Expected: prob_true=[0, 0.5, 1], prob_pred=[0.1, 0.5, 0.9]

import sys
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

# Mocking Django imports and settings since we aren't in a full Django environment
import django
from django.conf import settings
if not settings.configured:
    settings.configure()
    django.setup()

from django.contrib.admin.options import ModelAdmin

class MockInline:
    def __init__(self, model, admin_site):
        self.model = model
        self.admin_site = admin_site
    def has_view_or_change_permission(self, request, obj): return True
    def has_add_permission(self, request, obj): return True
    def has_delete_permission(self, request, obj): return True

class MockAdmin(ModelAdmin):
    inlines = [MockInline]
    # Override check to avoid needing a full Django setup for checks
    def check(self, **kwargs):
        return []

def test_get_inline_instances():
    model = MagicMock()
    admin_site = MagicMock()
    admin = MockAdmin(model, admin_site)
    request = MagicMock()
    
    # Test default behavior
    instances = admin.get_inline_instances(request)
    assert len(instances) == 1
    assert isinstance(instances[0], MockInline)
    print("Default behavior passed")

class OverrideAdmin(MockAdmin):
    def get_inlines(self, request, obj=None):
        if request.user.is_superuser:
            return [MockInline]
        else:
            return []

def test_override_get_inline_instances():
    model = MagicMock()
    admin_site = MagicMock()
    admin = OverrideAdmin(model, admin_site)
    
    # Superuser
    request_super = MagicMock()
    request_super.user.is_superuser = True
    instances_super = admin.get_inline_instances(request_super)
    assert len(instances_super) == 1
    print("Superuser override passed")
    
    # Non-superuser
    request_normal = MagicMock()
    request_normal.user.is_superuser = False
    instances_normal = admin.get_inline_instances(request_normal)
    assert len(instances_normal) == 0
    print("Normal user override passed")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_get_inline_instances()
        test_override_get_inline_instances()
        print("All tests passed!")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Tests failed: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        sys.exit(1)

class RenameFieldDBColTest(OperationTests):
    def test_rename_field_noop_with_db_column(self):
        """
        RenameField with db_column should be a noop.
        """
        app_label = "test_rnfl_dbcol"
        project_state = self.set_up_test_model(app_label)
        
        # 1. Change db_column of 'pink' to 'pink_col'
        operation_dbcol = migrations.AlterField(
            "Pony",
            "pink",
            models.IntegerField(default=3, db_column="pink_col"),
        )
        new_state_dbcol = project_state.clone()
        operation_dbcol.state_forwards(app_label, new_state_dbcol)
        
        with connection.schema_editor() as editor:
            operation_dbcol.database_forwards(app_label, editor, project_state, new_state_dbcol)
        
        # Now we have 'pink' field with 'pink_col' in DB.
        self.assertColumnExists(f"{app_label}_pony", "pink_col")
        self.assertColumnNotExists(f"{app_label}_pony", "pink")
        
        # 2. Rename 'pink' to 'blue' (db_column stays 'pink_col')
        operation_rename = migrations.RenameField("Pony", "pink", "blue")
        new_state_rename = new_state_dbcol.clone()
        operation_rename.state_forwards(app_label, new_state_rename)
        
        # We mock the schema_editor to see if alter_field is called
        mock_editor = MagicMock()
        # We need to make sure mock_editor behaves like a schema_editor if needed, 
        # but we only care if alter_field is called.
        
        # But RenameField.database_forwards uses the passed editor.
        # Let's use the real editor but wrap alter_field.
        with connection.schema_editor() as editor:

            operation_rename.database_forwards(app_label, editor, new_state_dbcol, new_state_rename)
            
            # Check if alter_field was called
            # According to the issue, it should NOT be called because it's a noop.
            self.assertEqual(editor.alter_field.call_count, 0, "alter_field should not be called when db_column remains the same")

import numpy as np

def two_sum_same_sign(a, b):
    x = a + b
    eb = x - a
    ea = x - eb
    eb = b - eb
    ea = a - ea
    return x, ea + eb

def two_diff(a, b):
    # a and b have same sign, and |a| >= |b|
    s = a - b
    v = s - a
    u = s - v
    uu = a - u
    vv = b - v
    return s, uu + vv

def two_sum_robust(a, b):
    if a == 0: return b, 0.0
    if b == 0: return a, 0.0
    
    if (a > 0 and b > 0) or (a < 0 and b < 0):
        return two_sum_same_sign(a, b)
    else:
        # opposite signs
        if abs(a) >= abs(b):
            if a > 0: # b < 0
                return two_diff(a, -b)
            else: # a < 0, b > 0
                s, err = two_diff(-a, b)
                return -s, -err
        else: # abs(b) > abs(a)
            if b > 0: # a < 0
                return two_diff(b, -a)
            else: # b < 0, a > 0
                s, err = two_diff(-b, a)
                return -s, -err

f1 = -3.089785075544792e+307
f2 = 1.7976931348623157e+308

res1 = two_sum_robust(f1, f2)
res2 = two_sum_robust(f2, f1)

print(f"f1: {f1}")
print(f"f2: {f2}")
print(f"two_sum_robust(f1, f2): {res1}")
print(f"two_sum_robust(f2, f1): {res2}")

np.testing.assert_equal(res1, res2)

import os
import django
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models
from django.contrib import admin
from django.core.checks import run_checks
import sys

# Configure settings
if not settings.configured:
    settings.configure(
        INSTALLED_APPS=[
            'django.contrib.admin',
            'django.contrib.auth',
            'django.contrib.contenttypes',
            'django.contrib.sessions',
            'testapp',
        ],
        DATABASES={'default': {'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.sqlite3', 'NAME': ':memory:'}},
        SECRET_KEY='secret',
        ROOT_URLCONF='testapp.urls',
    )
    django.setup()

# Define models
class Question(models.Model):
    question_text = models.CharField(max_length=200)

    class Meta:
        app_label = 'testapp'

class Choice(models.Model):
    question = models.ForeignKey(Question, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    choice_text = models.CharField(max_length=200)

    class Meta:
        app_label = 'testapp'

# Define admin
class QuestionAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    model = Question
    list_display = ["question_text", "choice_set"]

# Register admin
admin.site.register(Question, QuestionAdmin)
admin.site.register(Choice)

# Run system checks
# We use tags=['admin'] to only run admin checks
errors = run_checks(tags=['admin'])

print("--- Checks for reverse FK ---")
for error in errors:
    print(f"Error ID: {error.id}")
    print(f"Error Message: {error.msg}")

# Inspect choice_set
choice_set = getattr(Question, 'choice_set')
print(f"Type of choice_set: {type(choice_set)}")

# Also try with a ManyToManyField to see if E109 is triggered
class QuestionMM(models.Model):
    question_text = models.CharField(max_length=200)

    class Meta:
        app_label = 'testapp'

class ChoiceMM(models.Model):
    question = models.ManyToManyField(QuestionMM)
    choice_text = models.CharField(max_length=200)

    class Meta:
        app_label = 'testapp'

class QuestionMMAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    model = QuestionMM
    list_display = ["question_text", "choicemm_set"]

admin.site.register(QuestionMM, QuestionMMAdmin)

print("\n--- Checks for M2M ---")
errors_mm = run_checks(tags=['admin'])
for error in errors_mm:
    print(f"Error ID: {error.id}")
    print(f"Error Message: {error.msg}")

            else:
                if fpr[-1] > fpr_upper:
                    # Interpolate tpr at fpr_upper
                    i = np.searchsorted(fpr, fpr_upper) - 1
                    tpr_upper = np.interp(fpr_upper, [fpr[i], fpr[i+1]], [tpr[i], tpr[i+1]])

                    tpr_subset = np.append(tpr[idx], tpr_upper)
                else:
                    fpr_subset = fpr
                    tpr_subset = tpr
                auc_value = auc(fpr_subset, tpr_subset)

            # Standard AUC
            auc_value = auc(fpr, tpr)

        return auc_value
